title: Nice Apron, But Upside-Down-Printed “Cheat Sheet” Has Limited Usefulness
text:
Nice Apron, But Upside-Down-Printed “Cheat Sheet” Has Limited Usefulness. This DII “MEASURE UP” CHEF’S PRINTED APRON (28” x 35”) would be a lot more fun if the upside-down-printed “Cheat Sheet” had a better selection of reference information. Why would you want to know the F. and C. equivalents for oven temperatures? Or the pinch, dash, and smidge amounts in teaspoons?

Also, the charts that are moderately useful aren’t presented well. For example, the equivalents for liquids are hard to read, because the larger amounts (e.g., 2 cups) are shown at the bottom of the cup graphic, rather than at the top (as if the graphic cup were filled with liquid). The vegetable cooking times chart is fairly useful, except that it doesn’t mention the quantity of vegetables being cooked.

Otherwise, the adult-sized apron is exactly what I needed for cooking with my new Instant Pot. (The IP tends to spatter oil during sauteing.) The bib covers my front completely, as long as I adjust the bib height by pulling on the black ties after putting the apron on over my head. The body of the apron, with the pockets, wraps around my sides and covers the rest of my clothing.

The apron includes a hanging loop. You need this because the ties and the loop that goes over your head are actually one long piece of black material that is threaded through casings on the sides of the apron. Once you get the head loop adjusted correctly for your size, you don’t want to hang the apron by the head loop.

The apron is washable, and I’m sure that the printed “Cheat Sheet” will wash out eventually. (My apron hasn’t been washed, so I don’t know how long the print will last.) However, the apron will still be functional long after the print is gone.
